def compose(p: Perm, q: Perm) -> Perm:
    """Composite ``p`` then ``q`` (left-to-right), i.e. i |-> q[p[i]]."""
    return tuple(q[p[i]] for i in range(len(p)))


def inverse(p: Perm) -> Perm:
    """Inverse permutation."""
    out = [0] * len(p)
    for i, pi in enumerate(p):
        out[pi] = i
    return tuple(out)


class Group:
    """A finite group given by permutation generators, with cached structure."""

    def __init__(self, name: str, degree: int, generators: Sequence[Perm]) -> None:
        self.name: str = name
        self.degree: int = degree
        self.generators: List[Perm] = [tuple(g) for g in generators]
        self.identity: Perm = tuple(range(degree))
        self.elements: List[Perm] = self._close()
        self.index_of: Dict[Perm, int] = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(self.elements)}

    def _close(self) -> List[Perm]:
        seen = {self.identity}
        frontier = deque([self.identity])
        while frontier:
            g = frontier.popleft()
            for s in self.generators:
                h = compose(g, s)
                if h not in seen:
                    seen.add(h)
                    frontier.append(h)
        return sorted(seen)

    @property
    def order(self) -> int:
        return len(self.elements)

    def element_order(self, g: Perm) -> int:
        n, h = 1, g
        while h != self.identity:
            h = compose(h, g)
            n += 1
        return n

    def is_abelian(self) -> bool:
        return all(
            compose(a, b) == compose(b, a) for a in self.elements for b in self.elements
        )

    def centre(self) -> List[Perm]:
        return [
            z
            for z in self.elements
            if all(compose(z, g) == compose(g, z) for g in self.elements)
        ]

    def fingerprint(self) -> Tuple[int, Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...], bool]:
        """A canonical invariant separating all groups used in this script:
        (order, sorted multiset of element orders, commutativity)."""
        orders = Counter(self.element_order(g) for g in self.elements)
        return (self.order, tuple(sorted(orders.items())), self.is_abelian())

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.name}(order {self.order})"


def cyclic(n: int) -> Group:
    """Z/n as the rotation group of n points."""
    return Group(f"Z/{n}", n, [tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))])


def symmetric(n: int) -> Group:
    """S_n, generated by a transposition and an n-cycle."""
    transposition = tuple([1, 0] + list(range(2, n)))
    cycle = tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))
    return Group(f"S_{n}", n, [transposition, cycle])


def dihedral(n: int) -> Group:
    """Dihedral group of order 2n acting on the vertices of an n-gon."""
    rot = tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))
    refl = tuple((-i) % n for i in range(n))
    return Group(f"D_{n}", n, [rot, refl])


def klein_four() -> Group:
    """Z/2 x Z/2 acting on 4 points."""
    a = (1, 0, 3, 2)
    b = (2, 3, 0, 1)
    return Group("Z/2 x Z/2", 4, [a, b])


def quaternion8() -> Group:
    """The quaternion group Q_8 as a regular permutation group on 8 points."""
    # elements 1,-1,i,-i,j,-j,k,-k encoded as 0..7 with a multiplication table
    names = ["1", "-1", "i", "-i", "j", "-j", "k", "-k"]
    # multiplication on {+-1, +-i, +-j, +-k}
    base = {
        ("i", "i"): "-1",
        ("j", "j"): "-1",
        ("k", "k"): "-1",
        ("i", "j"): "k",
        ("j", "k"): "i",
        ("k", "i"): "j",
        ("j", "i"): "-k",
        ("k", "j"): "-i",
        ("i", "k"): "-j",
    }

    def split(x: str) -> Tuple[int, str]:
        return (-1, x[1:]) if x.startswith("-") else (1, x)

    def mul(x: str, y: str) -> str:
        sx, ux = split(x)
        sy, uy = split(y)
        s = sx * sy
        if ux == "1":
            u, extra = uy, 1
        elif uy == "1":
            u, extra = ux, 1
        else:
            r = base[(ux, uy)]
            sr, u = split(r)
            extra = sr
        s *= extra
        return u if s == 1 else "-" + u

    idx = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(names)}

    def perm_of(x: str) -> Perm:
        return tuple(idx[mul(names[i], x)] for i in range(8))

    return Group("Q_8", 8, [perm_of("i"), perm_of("j")])


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Homomorphisms: enumeration by generator lifting
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Hom = Tuple[Perm, ...]  # image of G.elements[i] is hom[i]


def _lift(G: Group, H: Group, images: Sequence[Perm]) -> Hom | None:
    """Try to extend an assignment of images of G's generators to all of G by a
    breadth-first walk over the Cayley graph; return None on any conflict."""
    phi: Dict[Perm, Perm] = {G.identity: H.identity}
    frontier = deque([G.identity])
    while frontier:
        g = frontier.popleft()
        for s, img in zip(G.generators, images):
            gs = compose(g, s)
            val = compose(phi[g], img)
            if gs in phi:
                if phi[gs] != val:
                    return None
            else:
                phi[gs] = val
                frontier.append(gs)
    return tuple(phi[g] for g in G.elements)


def homomorphisms(G: Group, H: Group) -> List[Hom]:
    """All group homomorphisms G -> H, as tuples indexed by ``G.elements``."""
    found: List[Hom] = []
    for images in product(H.elements, repeat=len(G.generators)):
        phi = _lift(G, H, images)
        if phi is None:
            continue
        # verify on the full multiplication table
        ok = all(
            phi[G.index_of[compose(a, b)]] == compose(phi[i], phi[G.index_of[b]])
            for i, a in enumerate(G.elements)
            for b in G.elements
        )
        if ok and phi not in found:
            found.append(phi)
    return found


def conjugate(H: Group, u: Perm, phi: Hom) -> Hom:
    """The conjugated homomorphism  a |-> u phi(a) u^{-1}."""
    ui = inverse(u)
    return tuple(compose(compose(ui, x), u) for x in phi)
    # note: with left-to-right composition, u x u^{-1} is compose(compose(ui, x), u)


def conjugacy_classes_of_homs(G: Group, H: Group) -> List[List[Hom]]:
    """Partition Hom(G,H) into conjugation orbits = homotopy classes of maps."""
    remaining = list(homomorphisms(G, H))
    classes: List[List[Hom]] = []
    while remaining:
        phi = remaining[0]
        orbit = {conjugate(H, u, phi) for u in H.elements}
        classes.append(sorted(orbit))
        remaining = [p for p in remaining if p not in orbit]
    return classes


def image(phi: Hom) -> FrozenSet[Perm]:
    return frozenset(phi)


def centralizer(H: Group, subset: Iterable[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """C_H(S) = elements of H commuting with every element of S."""
    S = list(subset)
    return [u for u in H.elements if all(compose(u, s) == compose(s, u) for s in S)]


def is_isomorphism(G: Group, H: Group, phi: Hom) -> bool:
    """A homomorphism is an isomorphism iff it is injective and surjective."""
    return len(set(phi)) == G.order and set(phi) == set(H.elements)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1-types: pi_0 together with the fundamental groups of the components
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


class OneType:
    """A homotopy 1-type, recorded by the fundamental groups of its components.

    By the classification theorem this multiset of groups (equivalently, pi_0
    together with the family of fundamental groups) is a complete invariant.
    """

    def __init__(self, name: str, components: Sequence[Group]) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.components = list(components)

    @property
    def pi0(self) -> int:
        return len(self.components)

    def invariant(self) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...], bool], ...]:
        return tuple(sorted(g.fingerprint() for g in self.components))

    def homotopy_equivalent(self, other: "OneType") -> bool:
        return self.invariant() == other.invariant()

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        inside = " ⊔ ".join(f"K({g.name},1)" for g in self.components) or "∅"
        return f"{self.name} = {inside}"

def rule(title: str) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def demo_classification_table(pairs: Sequence[Tuple[Group, Group]]) -> None:
    rule("1. [K(G,1), K(H,1)] = Hom(G,H)/conjugation, and the fibre count")
    print(
        f"{'G':>10} {'H':>10} {'|Hom|':>7} {'[K(G,1),K(H,1)]':>17} "
        f"{'orbit sizes':>24} {'= centraliser indices':>24}"
    )
    for G, H in pairs:
        classes = conjugacy_classes_of_homs(G, H)
        total = sum(len(c) for c in classes)
        orbit_sizes = [len(c) for c in classes]
        indices = [H.order // len(centralizer(H, image(c[0]))) for c in classes]
        assert orbit_sizes == indices, "fibre-count theorem violated"
        assert total == len(homomorphisms(G, H)), "counting identity violated"
        print(
            f"{G.name:>10} {H.name:>10} {total:>7} {len(classes):>17} "
            f"{str(sorted(orbit_sizes)):>24} {str(sorted(indices)):>24}"
        )
    print(
        "\nEvery row confirms:  |Hom(G,H)| = sum of centraliser indices, one per\n"
        "homotopy class of maps K(G,1) -> K(H,1)."
    )


def demo_fibres_in_detail(G: Group, H: Group) -> None:
    rule(f"2. Fibres in detail:  maps K({G.name},1) -> K({H.name},1)")
    classes = conjugacy_classes_of_homs(G, H)
    print(f"|Hom({G.name},{H.name})| = {sum(len(c) for c in classes)}")
    print(f"number of homotopy classes of maps = {len(classes)}\n")
    for k, orbit in enumerate(classes):
        rep = orbit[0]
        img = image(rep)
        cent = centralizer(H, img)
        idx = H.order // len(cent)
        kind = (
            "trivial map"
            if len(img) == 1
            else ("isomorphism" if is_isomorphism(G, H, rep) else "non-trivial")
        )
        print(
            f"  class {k}: |image| = {len(img):>3}   |C_H(image)| = {len(cent):>3}   "
            f"index = {idx:>3}   |orbit| = {len(orbit):>3}   ({kind})"
        )
        assert idx == len(orbit)
    print(
        "\nThe number of homomorphisms above a single homotopy class is exactly the\n"
        "index of the centraliser of the image: rigid maps (trivial image) have a\n"
        "one-element fibre; maps onto a centreless subgroup have the largest fibres."
    )


def demo_abelian_target(G: Group, H: Group) -> None:
    rule(f"3. Abelian target: conjugation acts trivially, {H.name} abelian")
    classes = conjugacy_classes_of_homs(G, H)
    total = sum(len(c) for c in classes)
    print(f"{H.name} abelian? {H.is_abelian()}")
    print(f"|Hom({G.name},{H.name})| = {total},  homotopy classes = {len(classes)}")
    assert total == len(classes)
    print(
        "Every orbit is a singleton, so [K(G,1), K(H,1)] = Hom(G,H) on the nose:\n"
        "with an abelian target there is no conjugacy quotient to take."
    )


def demo_whitehead(G: Group, H: Group) -> None:
    rule(f"4. Whitehead for 1-types:  K({G.name},1) vs K({H.name},1)")
    homs = homomorphisms(G, H)
    isos = [p for p in homs if is_isomorphism(G, H, p)]
    print(f"|Hom| = {len(homs)},  of which isomorphisms: {len(isos)}")
    equivalent = len(isos) > 0
    print(f"Some homomorphism induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups: {equivalent}")
    print(
        f"Hence K({G.name},1) and K({H.name},1) are homotopy equivalent: {equivalent}\n"
        "(a map of connected 1-types is a homotopy equivalence precisely when it is\n"
        "an isomorphism on fundamental groups)."
    )
    same_fp = G.fingerprint() == H.fingerprint()
    print(f"Cross-check by canonical group invariant: {same_fp}")
    assert same_fp == equivalent


def demo_non_isomorphic_same_order() -> None:
    rule("5. Same order, different homotopy type: K(Z/8,1), K(D_4,1), K(Q_8,1)")
    groups = [cyclic(8), dihedral(4), quaternion8()]
    for A in groups:
        for B in groups:
            homs = homomorphisms(A, B)
            isos = [p for p in homs if is_isomorphism(A, B, p)]
            mark = "≃" if isos else "≄"
            print(
                f"  K({A.name},1) {mark} K({B.name},1)   "
                f"(|Hom| = {len(homs):>3}, isomorphisms = {len(isos):>3})"
            )
    print(
        "\nAll three groups have order 8, so the three aspherical spaces have the\n"
        "same 'size', yet no two distinct ones are homotopy equivalent: the\n"
        "fundamental group, not its order, is the complete invariant."
    )


def demo_pi0_and_completeness() -> None:
    rule("6. Arbitrary 1-types: pi_0 plus the fundamental groups of the components")
    Z2, Z3, Z4 = cyclic(2), cyclic(3), cyclic(4)
    S3 = symmetric(3)
    X = OneType("X", [Z2, Z3, S3])
    Y = OneType("Y", [S3, Z3, Z2])  # same multiset, listed differently
    Z = OneType("Z", [Z2, Z4, S3])  # one component changed
    W = OneType("W", [Z2, Z3])  # one component removed
    for A, B in [(X, Y), (X, Z), (X, W)]:
        verdict = "homotopy equivalent" if A.homotopy_equivalent(B) else "NOT equivalent"
        print(f"  {A}\n  {B}\n    pi_0: {A.pi0} vs {B.pi0}  ->  {verdict}\n")
    assert X.homotopy_equivalent(Y)
    assert not X.homotopy_equivalent(Z)
    assert not X.homotopy_equivalent(W)
    print(
        "Two 1-types are homotopy equivalent exactly when some bijection of their\n"
        "component sets matches up the fundamental groups: reordering is harmless,\n"
        "changing one group or deleting a component is not."
    )


def demo_sharpness() -> None:
    rule("7. Sharpness: all homotopy groups agree, spaces do not")
    trivial = Group("1", 1, [])
    point = OneType("point", [trivial])
    two_points = OneType("two-point discrete space", [trivial, trivial])
    print("A totally disconnected space has *every* homotopy group trivial:")
    print("  a cube is connected, its continuous image is connected, and a")
    print("  connected subset of a totally disconnected space is a single point,")
    print("  so every based cube map is constant.\n")
    print("  pi_n(point)      = trivial for all n >= 1")
    print("  pi_n(two points) = trivial for all n >= 1")
    print(f"  pi_0(point) = {point.pi0},  pi_0(two points) = {two_points.pi0}")
    print(f"  homotopy equivalent? {point.homotopy_equivalent(two_points)}")
    assert not point.homotopy_equivalent(two_points)
    print(
        "\nSo no family of homotopy groups whatsoever - not merely pi_1 - can be a\n"
        "complete invariant without a connectivity hypothesis.  The component set\n"
        "is exactly the missing datum, and adding it restores completeness."
    )


def main() -> None:
    Z2, Z3, Z4, Z6 = cyclic(2), cyclic(3), cyclic(4), cyclic(6)
    V4 = klein_four()
    S3, S4 = symmetric(3), symmetric(4)
    D4 = dihedral(4)
    Q8 = quaternion8()

    print(__doc__)

    demo_classification_table(
        [
            (Z2, S3),
            (Z3, S3),
            (Z4, S4),
            (Z6, S3),
            (S3, S3),
            (V4, S4),
            (Z2, D4),

    demo_whitehead(V4, klein_four())
    demo_non_isomorphic_same_order()
    demo_pi0_and_completeness()
    demo_sharpness()

    rule("All assertions passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import deque
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]


def compose(p: Perm, q: Perm) -> Perm:
    """Composite 'p then q': i |-> q[p[i]]."""
    return tuple(q[p[i]] for i in range(len(p)))


def inverse(p: Perm) -> Perm:
    out = [0] * len(p)
    for i, pi in enumerate(p):
        out[pi] = i
    return tuple(out)


def closure(degree: int, gens: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    identity = tuple(range(degree))
    seen = {identity}
    frontier = deque([identity])
    while frontier:
        g = frontier.popleft()
        for s in gens:
            h = compose(g, s)
            if h not in seen:
                seen.add(h)
                frontier.append(h)
    return sorted(seen)


class Group:
    def __init__(self, name: str, degree: int, gens: Sequence[Perm]) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.degree = degree
        self.identity: Perm = tuple(range(degree))
        self.elements: List[Perm] = closure(degree, [tuple(g) for g in gens])

    @property
    def order(self) -> int:
        return len(self.elements)

    def element_order(self, g: Perm) -> int:
        n, h = 1, g
        while h != self.identity:
            h = compose(h, g)
            n += 1
        return n

    def conjugacy_classes(self) -> List[List[Perm]]:
        remaining = list(self.elements)
        out: List[List[Perm]] = []
        while remaining:
            g = remaining[0]
            orbit = {compose(compose(inverse(u), g), u) for u in self.elements}
            out.append(sorted(orbit))
            remaining = [x for x in remaining if x not in orbit]
        return out

    def centralizer_order(self, g: Perm) -> int:
        return sum(
            1 for u in self.elements if compose(u, g) == compose(g, u)
        )


def cyclic(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(f"Z/{n}", n, [tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))])


def symmetric(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(
        f"S_{n}",
        n,
        [tuple([1, 0] + list(range(2, n))), tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))],
    )


def dihedral(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(
        f"D_{n}",
        n,
        [tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n)), tuple((-i) % n for i in range(n))],
    )


def maps_from_cyclic(H: Group, n: int) -> int:
    """Number of homotopy classes of maps K(Z/n,1) -> K(H,1):
    conjugacy classes of elements of order dividing n (n = 0 means: no
    condition, i.e. the source is the circle with fundamental group Z)."""
    return sum(
        1
        for cls in H.conjugacy_classes()
        if n == 0 or n % H.element_order(cls[0]) == 0
    )


def homs_from_cyclic(H: Group, n: int) -> int:
    """|Hom(Z/n, H)| = number of elements of order dividing n."""
    return sum(1 for g in H.elements if n == 0 or n % H.element_order(g) == 0)


def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__)
    targets = [cyclic(6), symmetric(3), dihedral(4), symmetric(4)]

    print(f"{'H':>8} {'|H|':>5} {'classes of H':>13} " + "".join(
        f"{'n=' + str(n):>8}" for n in [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 0]
    ))
    for H in targets:
        classes = H.conjugacy_classes()
        row = "".join(f"{maps_from_cyclic(H, n):>8}" for n in [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 0])
        print(f"{H.name:>8} {H.order:>5} {len(classes):>13} {row}")
    print(
        "\nColumn n gives the number of homotopy classes of maps K(Z/n,1) -> K(H,1);\n"
        "the column n=0 is the circle, and it always equals the number of conjugacy\n"
        "classes of H — the free homotopy classes of loops in K(H,1)."
    )

    print("\nClass equation check (|H| = sum of centraliser indices):")
    for H in targets:
        indices = [H.order // H.centralizer_order(c[0]) for c in H.conjugacy_classes()]
        total = sum(indices)
        assert total == H.order
        assert all(
            idx == len(c) for idx, c in zip(indices, H.conjugacy_classes())
        )
        print(f"  {H.name:>6}: {' + '.join(map(str, indices))} = {total} = |{H.name}|")

    print("\nFibre check for the circle: each free homotopy class of loops in K(H,1)")
    print("contains exactly [H : C_H(g)] based loops, one for each conjugate of g.")
    for H in targets:
        ok = all(
            len(c) == H.order // H.centralizer_order(c[0]) for c in H.conjugacy_classes()
        )
        assert ok
        print(f"  {H.name:>6}: verified on all {len(H.conjugacy_classes())} classes")

    print("\nAll assertions passed.")

This module turns that theorem into a concrete algorithm in three stages:

  (1) ENUMERATE  Hom(G,H) by generator lifting over the Cayley graph of G;
  (2) PARTITION  Hom(G,H) into conjugation orbits (= homotopy classes);
  (3) CERTIFY    each orbit size against the index of the centraliser of the
                 image, which the fibre theorem predicts exactly.

Complexity: stage (1) costs O(|H|^{|S|} * |G| * |S|) for a generating set S of
G; stage (2) costs O(|Hom(G,H)| * |H| * |G|); stage (3) costs O(k * |H| * |G|)

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]
Hom = Tuple[Perm, ...]


def compose(p: Perm, q: Perm) -> Perm:
    """Composite 'p then q' (left-to-right): i |-> q[p[i]]."""
    return tuple(q[p[i]] for i in range(len(p)))


def inverse(p: Perm) -> Perm:
    out = [0] * len(p)
    for i, pi in enumerate(p):
        out[pi] = i
    return tuple(out)


@dataclass
class Group:
    """A finite permutation group: a name, a degree and generators."""

    name: str
    degree: int
    generators: List[Perm]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.identity: Perm = tuple(range(self.degree))
        self.elements: List[Perm] = self._close()
        self.index_of: Dict[Perm, int] = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(self.elements)}

    def _close(self) -> List[Perm]:
        seen = {self.identity}
        frontier = deque([self.identity])
        while frontier:
            g = frontier.popleft()
            for s in self.generators:
                h = compose(g, s)
                if h not in seen:
                    seen.add(h)
                    frontier.append(h)
        return sorted(seen)

    @property
    def order(self) -> int:
        return len(self.elements)


def lift_from_generators(G: Group, H: Group, images: Sequence[Perm]) -> Optional[Hom]:
    """Stage (1), inner loop.

    Try to extend the assignment ``generator_i |-> images[i]`` to a homomorphism
    by breadth-first propagation over the Cayley graph of G.  Returns the full
    homomorphism (indexed by ``G.elements``) or None if a conflict appears.
    """
    phi: Dict[Perm, Perm] = {G.identity: H.identity}
    frontier = deque([G.identity])
    while frontier:
        g = frontier.popleft()
        for s, img in zip(G.generators, images):
            gs = compose(g, s)
            val = compose(phi[g], img)
            if gs in phi:
                if phi[gs] != val:
                    return None
            else:
                phi[gs] = val
                frontier.append(gs)
    return tuple(phi[g] for g in G.elements)


def homomorphisms(G: Group, H: Group) -> List[Hom]:
    """Stage (1): all homomorphisms G -> H."""
    out: List[Hom] = []
    seen = set()
    for images in product(H.elements, repeat=len(G.generators)):
        phi = lift_from_generators(G, H, images)
        if phi is None or phi in seen:
            continue
        valid = all(
            phi[G.index_of[compose(a, b)]] == compose(phi[i], phi[G.index_of[b]])
            for i, a in enumerate(G.elements)
            for b in G.elements
        )
        if valid:
            seen.add(phi)
            out.append(phi)
    return out


def conjugate(u: Perm, phi: Hom) -> Hom:
    """The conjugated homomorphism a |-> u phi(a) u^{-1}."""
    ui = inverse(u)
    return tuple(compose(compose(ui, x), u) for x in phi)


def centralizer(H: Group, elements: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    return [
        u for u in H.elements if all(compose(u, s) == compose(s, u) for s in elements)
    ]


@dataclass
class HomotopyClass:
    """One homotopy class of maps K(G,1) -> K(H,1)."""

    representative: Hom
    orbit_size: int
    image_size: int
    centralizer_order: int
    centralizer_index: int

    @property
    def certified(self) -> bool:
        """The fibre theorem: |orbit| = [H : C_H(image)]."""
        return self.orbit_size == self.centralizer_index


def homotopy_classes(G: Group, H: Group) -> List[HomotopyClass]:
    """Stages (2) and (3): partition Hom(G,H) into homotopy classes and certify
    each orbit size against the index of the centraliser of the image."""
    remaining = homomorphisms(G, H)
    classes: List[HomotopyClass] = []
    while remaining:
        phi = remaining[0]
        orbit = {conjugate(u, phi) for u in H.elements}
        img = sorted(set(phi))
        cent = centralizer(H, img)
        classes.append(
            HomotopyClass(
                representative=phi,
                orbit_size=len(orbit),
                image_size=len(img),
                centralizer_order=len(cent),
                centralizer_index=H.order // len(cent),
            )
        )
        remaining = [p for p in remaining if p not in orbit]
    return classes


def cyclic(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(f"Z/{n}", n, [tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))])


def symmetric(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(
        f"S_{n}",
        n,
        [tuple([1, 0] + list(range(2, n))), tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))],
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Invariant = Tuple[int, Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...], bool]


class UnionFind:
    """Disjoint-set forest with path compression."""

    def __init__(self, items: Sequence[Hashable]) -> None:
        self.parent: Dict[Hashable, Hashable] = {x: x for x in items}

    def find(self, x: Hashable) -> Hashable:
        while self.parent[x] != x:
            self.parent[x] = self.parent[self.parent[x]]
            x = self.parent[x]
        return x

    def union(self, x: Hashable, y: Hashable) -> None:
        rx, ry = self.find(x), self.find(y)
        if rx != ry:
            self.parent[rx] = ry


@dataclass
class FiniteGroupData:
    """A finite group recorded by its multiplication table on 0..n-1."""

    name: str
    table: List[List[int]]

    @property
    def order(self) -> int:
        return len(self.table)

    def element_order(self, g: int) -> int:
        n, h, e = 1, g, self.identity
        while h != e:
            h = self.table[h][g]
            n += 1
        return n

    @property
    def identity(self) -> int:
        for e in range(self.order):
            if all(self.table[e][g] == g for g in range(self.order)):
                return e
        raise ValueError("no identity: not a group table")

    def is_abelian(self) -> bool:
        return all(
            self.table[a][b] == self.table[b][a]
            for a in range(self.order)
            for b in range(self.order)
        )

    def invariant(self) -> Invariant:
        """A canonical isomorphism invariant: order, multiset of element orders,
        commutativity.  (Replace by a full isomorphism test if the groups in
        play are not separated by these data.)"""
        orders = Counter(self.element_order(g) for g in range(self.order))
        return (self.order, tuple(sorted(orders.items())), self.is_abelian())


@dataclass
class Groupoid:
    """A finite 1-type presented as a groupoid: objects, a list of arrows given
    as (source, target) pairs, and the fundamental group attached to each
    object (all objects in a component carry isomorphic groups)."""

    objects: List[str]
    arrows: List[Tuple[str, str]]
    vertex_group: Dict[str, FiniteGroupData] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def components(self) -> List[List[str]]:
        """Stage (1): connected components via union-find over the arrows."""
        uf = UnionFind(self.objects)
        for s, t in self.arrows:
            uf.union(s, t)
        buckets: Dict[Hashable, List[str]] = {}
        for x in self.objects:
            buckets.setdefault(uf.find(x), []).append(x)
        return [sorted(v) for v in buckets.values()]

    def complete_invariant(self) -> Tuple[Invariant, ...]:
        """Stage (2): the sorted multiset of fundamental groups of components."""
        return tuple(
            sorted(self.vertex_group[comp[0]].invariant() for comp in self.components())
        )

    @property
    def pi0(self) -> int:
        return len(self.components())


def homotopy_equivalent(X: Groupoid, Y: Groupoid) -> bool:
    """Decide homotopy equivalence of two finite 1-types."""
    return X.complete_invariant() == Y.complete_invariant()

def compose(p: Perm, q: Perm) -> Perm:
    return tuple(q[p[i]] for i in range(len(p)))


def inverse(p: Perm) -> Perm:
    out = [0] * len(p)
    for i, pi in enumerate(p):

class Group:
    def __init__(self, name: str, degree: int, gens: Sequence[Perm]) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.degree = degree
        self.generators = [tuple(g) for g in gens]
        self.identity: Perm = tuple(range(degree))
        seen = {self.identity}
        frontier = deque([self.identity])
        while frontier:
            g = frontier.popleft()
            for s in self.generators:
                h = compose(g, s)
                if h not in seen:
                    seen.add(h)
                    frontier.append(h)
        self.elements: List[Perm] = sorted(seen)
        self.index_of: Dict[Perm, int] = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(self.elements)}

    @property
    def order(self) -> int:
        return len(self.elements)


def cyclic(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(f"Z/{n}", n, [tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))])


def symmetric(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(

        n,
        [tuple([1, 0] + list(range(2, n))), tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n))],
    )


def dihedral(n: int) -> Group:
    return Group(
        f"D{n}",
        n,
        [tuple((i + 1) % n for i in range(n)), tuple((-i) % n for i in range(n))],
    )


def klein() -> Group:
    return Group("V4", 4, [(1, 0, 3, 2), (2, 3, 0, 1)])


def lift(G: Group, H: Group, images: Sequence[Perm]) -> Optional[Hom]:
    phi: Dict[Perm, Perm] = {G.identity: H.identity}
    frontier = deque([G.identity])
    while frontier:
        g = frontier.popleft()
        for s, img in zip(G.generators, images):
            gs, val = compose(g, s), compose(phi[g], img)
            if gs in phi:
                if phi[gs] != val:
                    return None
            else:
                phi[gs] = val
                frontier.append(gs)
    return tuple(phi[g] for g in G.elements)


def homomorphisms(G: Group, H: Group) -> List[Hom]:
    out, seen = [], set()
    for images in product(H.elements, repeat=len(G.generators)):
        phi = lift(G, H, images)
        if phi is None or phi in seen:
            continue
        if all(
            phi[G.index_of[compose(a, b)]] == compose(phi[i], phi[G.index_of[b]])

            for b in G.elements

            seen.add(phi)
            out.append(phi)
    return out

    ui = inverse(u)
    return tuple(compose(compose(ui, x), u) for x in phi)


def centralizer_order(H: Group, elems: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    return sum(
        1 for u in H.elements if all(compose(u, s) == compose(s, u) for s in elems)
    )

        phi = remaining[0]
        orbit = {conjugate(u, phi) for u in H.elements}
        img = sorted(set(phi))
        out.append((len(orbit), H.order // centralizer_order(H, img), len(img)))
        remaining = [p for p in remaining if p not in orbit]
    return sorted(out)

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>Homotopy classes of maps between aspherical spaces</h1>
  <div class="sub">
    An aspherical space with fundamental group <i>G</i> — written <i>K</i>(<i>G</i>,1) — is completely
    determined by <i>G</i>. Maps between such spaces are determined too, but only up to a twist:
    two maps are homotopic exactly when the homomorphisms they induce differ by conjugation.
    Choose two groups and watch the correspondence being computed from scratch.
  </div>
  <div class="formula">
    [ <i>K</i>(<i>G</i>,1), <i>K</i>(<i>H</i>,1) ]  ≅  Hom(<i>G</i>,<i>H</i>) / conjugation,
       and each class contains exactly [ <i>H</i> : C<sub><i>H</i></sub>(image) ] homomorphisms
  </div>

  <div class="controls">
    <div>
      <label for="gsel">source group G  (space K(G,1))</label>
      <select id="gsel"></select>
    </div>
    <div>
      <label for="hsel">target group H  (space K(H,1))</label>
      <select id="hsel"></select>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="cards">
    <div class="card"><div class="big" id="cHom">–</div><div class="lab">homomorphisms G → H</div></div>
    <div class="card"><div class="big" id="cCls">–</div><div class="lab">homotopy classes of maps</div></div>
    <div class="card"><div class="big" id="cIso">–</div><div class="lab">isomorphisms (homotopy equivalences)</div></div>
    <div class="card"><div class="big" id="cEq">–</div><div class="lab">K(G,1) ≃ K(H,1)?</div></div>
  </div>

  <table id="tbl">
    <thead><tr>
      <th>class</th><th>|image|</th><th>|C<sub>H</sub>(image)|</th>
      <th>index [H : C<sub>H</sub>]</th><th>homomorphisms in class</th><th>fibre theorem</th><th>type</th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody></tbody>
  </table>

  <div class="grid" id="grid"></div>
  <div class="legend" id="legend"></div>

  <details>
    <summary>Why is a homotopy the same thing as a conjugation?</summary>
    <p>
      A map out of a connected aspherical space is rigid in a strong sense: it is determined by what
      it does to loops at a single basepoint. Suppose two maps <i>F</i> and <i>G</i> are given, and
      suppose there is one isomorphism <i>h</i> at the basepoint that intertwines their two actions on
      loops, i.e. <i>F</i>(<i>a</i>)·<i>h</i> = <i>h</i>·<i>G</i>(<i>a</i>) for every loop <i>a</i>.
      Then one can <em>propagate</em> <i>h</i> over the whole space: choose, for each point <i>X</i>, a
      path <i>p<sub>X</sub></i> from the basepoint, and set
      <i>h<sub>X</sub></i> = <i>F</i>(<i>p<sub>X</sub></i>)<sup>−1</sup>·<i>h</i>·<i>G</i>(<i>p<sub>X</sub></i>).
      Two different choices of path differ by a loop, and loops are intertwined by hypothesis, so the
      recipe does not depend on the choice — which is exactly what makes it a coherent homotopy.
      For maps whose source and target are single points of the algebraic model, <i>h</i> is just an
      element <i>u</i> of <i>H</i>, and the intertwining condition reads
      ψ(<i>a</i>) = <i>u</i><sup>−1</sup>φ(<i>a</i>)<i>u</i>: conjugation.
    </p>
  </details>

  <details>
    <summary>Where does the fibre count come from?</summary>
    <p>
      Conjugation makes <i>H</i> act on the set Hom(<i>G</i>,<i>H</i>), and a homotopy class of maps is
      exactly one orbit. An element <i>u</i> fixes φ precisely when it commutes with every element of
      the image of φ, i.e. when it lies in the centraliser C<sub><i>H</i></sub>(φ(<i>G</i>)). By the
      orbit–stabiliser theorem the orbit is the coset space <i>H</i>/C<sub><i>H</i></sub>(φ(<i>G</i>)),
      so its size is the index of that centraliser. Two extremes: the trivial homomorphism has
      centraliser all of <i>H</i>, so its class contains a single homomorphism — the constant map is
      rigid; and an isomorphism onto a centreless group has trivial centraliser, so a whole copy of
      <i>H</i> collapses into one homotopy class.
    </p>
  </details>

  <details>
    <summary>Why does this classify the spaces themselves?</summary>
    <p>
      Because of the one-dimensional Whitehead theorem: a map between connected aspherical spaces is a
      homotopy equivalence <em>if and only if</em> it induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups.
      The proof is a translation of three properties: injectivity on loops makes the map faithful,
      surjectivity makes it full, and connectedness of the target makes it essentially surjective.
      So the “K(G,1) ≃ K(H,1)?” indicator above is literally asking whether some homomorphism in the
      list is bijective.
    </p>
  </details>

  <div class="note">
    Every number in the table is computed in your browser: homomorphisms are found by lifting
    assignments of the generators over the Cayley graph of <i>G</i>, orbits are formed by conjugating,
    and centralisers are found by scanning <i>H</i>. The last column checks the identity
    “orbit size = centraliser index” on every single class, and the class sizes always sum to
    |Hom(<i>G</i>,<i>H</i>)|.
  </div>
</div>

<script>
// ---------- permutation groups ----------
function compose(p,q){const n=p.length,r=new Array(n);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)r[i]=q[p[i]];return r;}
function inverse(p){const n=p.length,r=new Array(n);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)r[p[i]]=i;return r;}
function key(p){return p.join(",");}

function makeGroup(name,degree,gens){
  const id=[...Array(degree).keys()];
  const seen=new Map([[key(id),id]]);
  const queue=[id];
  while(queue.length){
    const g=queue.shift();
    for(const s of gens){const h=compose(g,s);const k=key(h);if(!seen.has(k)){seen.set(k,h);queue.push(h);}}
  }
  const elements=[...seen.values()].sort((a,b)=>key(a)<key(b)?-1:1);
  const index=new Map(elements.map((e,i)=>[key(e),i]));
  return {name,degree,gens,id,elements,index,order:elements.length};
}
const cyc=n=>makeGroup("Z/"+n,n,[[...Array(n).keys()].map(i=>(i+1)%n)]);
const sym=n=>makeGroup("S"+n,n,[[1,0,...[...Array(n).keys()].slice(2)],[...Array(n).keys()].map(i=>(i+1)%n)]);
const dih=n=>makeGroup("D"+n+" (order "+(2*n)+")",n,[[...Array(n).keys()].map(i=>(i+1)%n),[...Array(n).keys()].map(i=>((n-i)%n))]);
const klein=()=>makeGroup("Z/2 × Z/2",4,[[1,0,3,2],[2,3,0,1]]);
function quaternion(){
  const names=["1","-1","i","-i","j","-j","k","-k"];
  const base={"i,i":"-1","j,j":"-1","k,k":"-1","i,j":"k","j,k":"i","k,i":"j","j,i":"-k","k,j":"-i","i,k":"-j"};
  const split=x=>x[0]==="-"?[-1,x.slice(1)]:[1,x];
  function mul(x,y){let[sx,ux]=split(x),[sy,uy]=split(y),s=sx*sy,u,e=1;
    if(ux==="1"){u=uy;}else if(uy==="1"){u=ux;}else{const r=base[ux+","+uy];const[sr,ur]=split(r);u=ur;e=sr;}
    s*=e;return s===1?u:"-"+u;}
  const idx={};names.forEach((n,i)=>idx[n]=i);
  const perm=x=>names.map(n=>idx[mul(n,x)]);
  return makeGroup("Q8",8,[perm("i"),perm("j")]);
}
const GROUPS=[cyc(2),cyc(3),cyc(4),cyc(5),cyc(6),cyc(8),klein(),sym(3),dih(4),quaternion(),sym(4)];

// ---------- homomorphisms by generator lifting ----------
function lift(G,H,images){
  const phi=new Map([[key(G.id),H.id]]);
  const queue=[G.id];
  while(queue.length){
    const g=queue.shift();const pg=phi.get(key(g));
    for(let i=0;i<G.gens.length;i++){
      const gs=compose(g,G.gens[i]),val=compose(pg,images[i]),k=key(gs);
      if(phi.has(k)){ if(key(phi.get(k))!==key(val)) return null; }
      else{ phi.set(k,val); queue.push(gs); }
    }
  }
  return G.elements.map(g=>phi.get(key(g)));
}
function homomorphisms(G,H){
  const out=[],seen=new Set();
  const total=Math.pow(H.order,G.gens.length);
  for(let t=0;t<total;t++){
    let m=t;const images=[];
    for(let i=0;i<G.gens.length;i++){images.push(H.elements[m%H.order]);m=Math.floor(m/H.order);}
    const phi=lift(G,H,images);
    if(!phi) continue;
    const kk=phi.map(key).join("|");
    if(seen.has(kk)) continue;
    let ok=true;
    for(let a=0;a<G.order&&ok;a++)for(let b=0;b<G.order&&ok;b++){
      const ab=G.index.get(key(compose(G.elements[a],G.elements[b])));
      if(key(phi[ab])!==key(compose(phi[a],phi[b]))) ok=false;
    }
    if(ok){seen.add(kk);out.push(phi);}
  }
  return out;
}
const conjugate=(u,phi)=>{const ui=inverse(u);return phi.map(x=>compose(compose(ui,x),u));};
function centralizer(H,elems){return H.elements.filter(u=>elems.every(s=>key(compose(u,s))===key(compose(s,u))));}

function analyse(G,H){
  const homs=homomorphisms(G,H);
  const keyOf=phi=>phi.map(key).join("|");
  const pending=new Map(homs.map(p=>[keyOf(p),p]));
  const classes=[];
  const classOf=new Map();
  while(pending.size){
    const phi=pending.values().next().value;
    const orbit=new Map();
    for(const u of H.elements){const c=conjugate(u,phi);orbit.set(keyOf(c),c);}
    const img=[...new Map(phi.map(x=>[key(x),x])).values()];
    const cent=centralizer(H,img);
    const idx=classes.length;
    for(const k of orbit.keys()){pending.delete(k);classOf.set(k,idx);}
    const isIso=(new Set(phi.map(key))).size===G.order && G.order===H.order;
    classes.push({size:orbit.size,imageSize:img.length,cent:cent.length,index:H.order/cent.length,iso:isIso,rep:phi});
  }
  classes.sort((a,b)=>a.imageSize-b.imageSize||a.size-b.size);
  return {homs,classes,order:homs.map(keyOf).map(k=>classOf.get(k))};
}

// ---------- rendering ----------
const gsel=document.getElementById("gsel"),hsel=document.getElementById("hsel");
GROUPS.forEach((g,i)=>{
  gsel.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend",`<option value="${i}">${g.name} — order ${g.order}</option>`);
  hsel.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend",`<option value="${i}">${g.name} — order ${g.order}</option>`);
});
gsel.value="7";hsel.value="7";

const palette=["#7cc4ff","#ffd479","#7ee2a8","#ff9ecb","#c3a0ff","#ffb27c","#9be7ff","#e0e07c","#ff8f8f","#8fffd7","#bdb2ff","#ffc6a5"];

function render(){
  const G=GROUPS[+gsel.value],H=GROUPS[+hsel.value];
  const t0=performance.now();
  const {homs,classes}=analyse(G,H);
  const ms=(performance.now()-t0).toFixed(0);
  const isoCount=homs.filter(p=>(new Set(p.map(key))).size===G.order&&G.order===H.order).length;
  document.getElementById("cHom").textContent=homs.length;
  document.getElementById("cCls").textContent=classes.length;
  document.getElementById("cIso").textContent=isoCount;
  const eq=isoCount>0;
  const eqEl=document.getElementById("cEq");
  eqEl.textContent=eq?"yes":"no";
  eqEl.style.color=eq?"var(--good)":"var(--bad)";

  const tb=document.querySelector("#tbl tbody");tb.innerHTML="";
  let total=0;
  classes.forEach((c,i)=>{
    total+=c.size;
    const type=c.imageSize===1?"constant map":(c.iso?"homotopy equivalence":"non-trivial");
    tb.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend",
      `<tr><td class="klass" style="color:${palette[i%palette.length]}">${i}</td>
       <td>${c.imageSize}</td><td>${c.cent}</td><td>${c.index}</td><td>${c.size}</td>
       <td><span class="chip ok">${c.size===c.index?"verified":"FAILED"}</span></td>
       <td>${type}</td></tr>`);
  });

  const grid=document.getElementById("grid");grid.innerHTML="";
  classes.forEach((c,i)=>{
    for(let k=0;k<c.size;k++){
      const d=document.createElement("div");
      d.className="dot";d.style.background=palette[i%palette.length];
      d.title=`class ${i} — one of ${c.size} homomorphisms realising the same map up to homotopy`;
      grid.appendChild(d);
    }
  });
  document.getElementById("legend").innerHTML =
    `Each square is one homomorphism ${G.name} → ${H.name}; squares of the same colour are the same map `+
    `up to homotopy. ${total} homomorphisms fall into ${classes.length} homotopy classes `+
    `(computed in ${ms} ms), and the class sizes ${classes.map(c=>c.index).join(" + ")} = ${total} `+
    `are exactly the centraliser indices.`;
}
gsel.addEventListener("change",render);
hsel.addEventListener("change",render);
render();
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    },
    {
      "title": "The Complete-Invariant Laboratory: pi_0 and the Fundamental Groups of the Components",
      "description": "Build two homotopy 1-types by assembling connected pieces - each piece an aspherical space with a chosen fundamental group - and ask whether they are the same shape. The verdict applies the classification theorem for arbitrary 1-types: they are homotopy equivalent exactly when some bijection of their component sets matches up the fundamental groups, and when a matching exists it is displayed explicitly, while a failure is diagnosed either as a mismatch of the number of components or as an unmatchable multiset of groups. Presets let the reader shuffle the pieces (still equivalent), change one piece (no longer equivalent), and load the sharpest counterexample in the subject - a point versus a two-point discrete space, which agree in every homotopy group yet differ in homotopy type. Expandable panels give the decomposition and gluing arguments, the three-line proof that all homotopy groups of a totally disconnected space vanish, and a reminder of which familiar spaces are aspherical.",
      "html": "<!DOCTYPE html>

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>The complete invariant of a homotopy 1-type</h1>
  <div class="sub">
    A homotopy 1-type is a space whose only interesting structure lives in dimension one: loops can be
    knotted together in complicated ways, but every sphere of dimension two or more can be shrunk to a
    point. Build two such spaces out of connected pieces and ask whether they are the same shape.
  </div>
  <div class="thm">
    <b>Classification theorem.</b> Two homotopy 1-types are homotopy equivalent if and only if there is a
    bijection between their sets of connected components under which the fundamental groups of
    corresponding components are isomorphic. In other words the complete invariant is the
    <i>multiset of fundamental groups of the components</i>: the set of components alone is not enough,
    and the fundamental groups alone are not enough either.
  </div>

  <div class="presets">
    <button data-preset="reorder">preset: the same pieces, shuffled</button>
    <button data-preset="swap">preset: one piece changed</button>
    <button data-preset="sharp">preset: a point versus two points</button>
    <button data-preset="clear">clear both</button>
  </div>

  <div class="lab">
    <div class="side">
      <h2>Space X</h2>
      <div class="row">
        <select id="selX"></select>
        <button data-add="X">add component</button>
      </div>
      <div class="comps" id="compsX"></div>
      <div class="stats" id="statX"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="side">
      <h2>Space Y</h2>
      <div class="row">
        <select id="selY"></select>
        <button data-add="Y">add component</button>
      </div>
      <div class="comps" id="compsY"></div>
      <div class="stats" id="statY"></div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="verdict" id="verdict"></div>

  <details>
    <summary>Why is this the right invariant? (the two halves of the proof)</summary>
    <p>
      <b>Decomposition.</b> Every 1-type is the disjoint union of its connected components: in the
      algebraic model one takes the full sub-object on each isomorphism class of points, and the
      obvious assembly map back into the whole is faithful (arrows never leave a component), full (a
      component is a full sub-object) and essentially surjective (every point lies in its own
      component). So the general case reduces to disjoint unions.
    </p>
    <p>
      <b>Gluing.</b> A disjoint union of connected 1-types is determined by its indexing set together
      with the fundamental groups of the pieces. Given a bijection of index sets and isomorphisms of
      the corresponding groups, one glues the component-wise homotopy equivalences supplied by the
      classification of connected 1-types. Conversely, an equivalence must permute the summands,
      because points in different components are never connected by a path, and it matches the
      fundamental groups of matched components.
    </p>
  </details>

  <details>
    <summary>The sharpness example: all homotopy groups agree, the spaces do not</summary>
    <p>
      Take the one-point space and the two-point discrete space. Both are totally disconnected, and in a
      totally disconnected space <em>every</em> homotopy group vanishes: a cube is connected, the
      continuous image of a connected set is connected, and a connected subset of a totally disconnected
      space is a single point — so every based cube map is constant. Hence
      π<sub>1</sub>, π<sub>2</sub>, π<sub>3</sub>, … all agree (all trivial), yet the two spaces are
      obviously not homotopy equivalent, since a homotopy equivalence between totally disconnected
      spaces is a bijection of points. The entire tower of homotopy groups is blind to the number of
      components; the classification theorem above says that once you add that number — and, in
      general, the fundamental groups indexed by it — nothing else is missing.
    </p>
    <table>
      <thead><tr><th>space</th><th>π₀</th><th>π₁</th><th>π₂, π₃, …</th><th>homotopy type</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>point</td><td>1</td><td>trivial</td><td>trivial</td><td>a point</td></tr>
        <tr><td>two-point discrete space</td><td>2</td><td>trivial</td><td>trivial</td><td>not a point</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </details>

  <details>
    <summary>What the pieces mean topologically</summary>
    <p>
      A connected 1-type with fundamental group <i>G</i> is an aspherical space <i>K</i>(<i>G</i>,1),
      and they are everywhere: the circle is a <i>K</i>(ℤ,1); a closed surface of genus at least one is

### A guided tour of homotopy 1-types, their maps, and their complete invariant

---

## 1. The question

Poincaré's fundamental group takes a space and returns a group: walk in a loop, come back,
and record what could not be undone by sliding. It is the first invariant every topologist
meets, and it is **lossy** — a sphere and a point both have trivial fundamental group.

So here is the question this page answers:

> **On which spaces does the fundamental group remember *everything*, and what exactly
> goes wrong at the boundary of that class?**

The answer is remarkably clean, and it goes far beyond a statement about spaces: it
classifies the **maps** between them, the **homotopies** between those maps, and it comes
with a counting formula. Along the way we will meet a counterexample so sharp that it
defeats not merely $\pi_1$ but the entire infinite tower $\pi_1, \pi_2, \pi_3, \dots$.

---

## 2. Aspherical spaces, and the algebra hiding inside them

A space is **aspherical** — an Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G,1)$, or a *homotopy 1-type* —
if loops can be interesting but every sphere of dimension $\ge 2$ can be shrunk to a point.
These are not exotic:

| space | fundamental group |
|---|---|
| the circle $S^1$ | $\mathbb{Z}$ |
| a closed surface of genus $g \ge 1$ | its surface group |
| configurations of $n$ points in the plane | the braid group $B_n$ |
| a complete manifold of non-positive curvature | its deck group |

For such a space, keeping only the **points** and the **homotopy classes of paths between
them** loses nothing. Paths compose, every path reverses, and going out and back is the same
as standing still: the result is a *groupoid*, and for a 1-type it is a faithful replacement
for the space. From here on, topology becomes algebra:

$$\text{point} \leftrightarrow \text{object},\qquad
\pi_1(X,x) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(x),\qquad
\text{map} \leftrightarrow \text{functor},\qquad
\text{homotopy} \leftrightarrow \text{natural isomorphism}.$$

<details>
<summary><b>Click for the precise dictionary and definitions</b></summary>

* A **groupoid** is a category in which every arrow is invertible.
* The **vertex group** $\mathrm{Aut}(c)$ at an object $c$ is the group of arrows $c \to c$;
  it is the fundamental group based at $c$. In a groupoid every endomorphism is already
  invertible, so this is also the endomorphism monoid.
* A groupoid is **connected at $c$** if every object admits an arrow from $c$ — the algebraic
  form of path-connectedness. A connected groupoid with vertex group $G$ *is* a $K(G,1)$.
* **Equivalence of categories** (full + faithful + essentially surjective) is the algebraic
  form of homotopy equivalence.
* $\pi_0$ is the set of isomorphism classes of objects: the set of connected components.

Useful background: [Eilenberg–MacLane space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilenberg%E2%80%93MacLane_space),
[fundamental groupoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_groupoid),
[aspherical space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aspherical_space).
</details>

The starting point of the whole story:

> **Theorem (connected 1-types are groups).** Two connected homotopy 1-types are homotopy
> equivalent if and only if their fundamental groups are isomorphic.

---

## 3. Play first: what does a *map* between two of these spaces look like?

Before any proofs, get your hands on the objects. The widget below computes, from scratch and
in your browser, all the maps between two aspherical spaces — by computing all the

3. Set source and target to two *different* groups of the same order, e.g. $D_4$ and $Q_8$.

Two patterns should jump out, and they are exactly the two theorems of the next section:
homomorphisms collapse into classes **by conjugation**, and the size of each class is the

---

## 4. The classification of maps

### 4.1 Every homomorphism is realized

> **Realization theorem.** Let $X$ be a connected 1-type with basepoint $x$, let $Y$ be any
> 1-type with a chosen point $y$. Then every homomorphism
> $\varphi : \pi_1(X,x) \to \pi_1(Y,y)$ is induced by an actual map $X \to Y$.

<details>
<summary><b>The construction, in three lines</b></summary>

Because $X$ is connected, choose once and for all a path $p_Z$ from the basepoint $x$ to every
point $Z$, taking $p_x$ to be the constant path. Any arrow $g : Z \to W$, however far from the
basepoint it lives, can then be *dragged home*:
$$\ell(g) = p_Z \cdot g \cdot p_W^{-1} \in \pi_1(X,x).$$
This operation sends identities to the identity and reverses composition order in the
bookkeeping way, so
$$R_\varphi(Z) = y \quad\text{for all } Z, \qquad R_\varphi(g) = \varphi(\ell(g))$$
is a genuine map of 1-types. And because $p_x$ is the constant path, $\ell(a) = a$ for a loop
$a$ at the basepoint, so $R_\varphi$ induces exactly $\varphi$. $\blacksquare$
</details>

### 4.2 Homotopies are conjugations

> **Homotopy criterion.** Let $X$ be connected at $x$ and let $F, G : X \to Y$ be maps. Then
> $F \simeq G$ if and only if there is a *single* isomorphism $h : F(x) \to G(x)$ with
> $$F(a)\, h = h\, G(a) \qquad \text{for every loop } a \text{ at } x.$$

<details>
<summary><b>Why one isomorphism at one point suffices (proof sketch)</b></summary>

One direction is a one-liner: a homotopy evaluated at the basepoint gives $h$, and naturality
is the displayed identity.

The other direction is where connectedness earns its keep. Define
$$h_Z = F(p_Z)^{-1}\, h\, G(p_Z).$$
The crucial check is **path-independence**: any other path $p'$ from $x$ to $Z$ differs from
$p_Z$ by a loop $a$, and the intertwining hypothesis applied to $a^{-1}$ shows that $p'$ gives
the same answer. Once the recipe is independent of the path, naturality is automatic: for an
arrow $f : Z \to W$, the composite $p_Z \cdot f$ is itself a legitimate path to $W$, and
computing $h_W$ with it turns naturality into a tautology. $\blacksquare$
</details>

Specializing to maps that collapse everything to a point, the isomorphism $h$ is just an
element $u$ of the target group, and the intertwining condition reads $\psi = u^{-1}\varphi u$.
That is the punchline:

$$\boxed{\;[\,K(G,1),\,K(H,1)\,] \;\cong\; \mathrm{Hom}(G,H)\big/\text{conjugation}\;}$$

The correspondence is compatible with composition: the homomorphism induced by a composite of
maps is conjugate to the composite of the induced homomorphisms, so on conjugacy classes it is
an exact identity. The residual conjugation is nothing but the familiar basepoint-change
ambiguity of unbased homotopy theory.

---

## 5. Counting: how many homomorphisms hide inside one map?

Conjugation makes $H$ act on $\mathrm{Hom}(G,H)$; a homotopy class of maps is one orbit. What
stabilizes $\varphi$? Exactly the elements commuting with everything in the image.

> **Fibre theorem.** The homomorphisms realizing a fixed homotopy class form the coset space
> $H / C_H(\varphi(G))$; in particular their number is the index $[H : C_H(\varphi(G))]$.
> Consequently $|\mathrm{Hom}(G,H)| = \sum_{[\varphi]} [H : C_H(\varphi(G))]$.

Extremes worth remembering: the constant map is *rigid* (its centraliser is all of $H$, so its
class has one element), while a surjection onto a centreless group has a fibre of size $|H|$.
With an abelian target, every fibre is a single point and no quotient is needed at all.

Here is the whole picture at once: how many maps exist between small aspherical spaces, how
the fibre theorem holds class by class, and how the counting identity decomposes
$|\mathrm{Hom}(G,H)|$ into centraliser indices.

And here is the pipeline that produces those numbers — enumeration by lifting generators over

## 6. Whitehead's theorem in one dimension

Does a map that induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups have to be a homotopy
equivalence? In general no — that is what higher homotopy is *for*. But on 1-types:

> **Whitehead theorem for 1-types.** A map between *connected* 1-types is a homotopy
> equivalence if and only if it induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups.

<details>
<summary><b>Three steps, each a translation of one property</b></summary>

* **Injective on $\pi_1$ $\Rightarrow$ faithful.** If two arrows have the same image, their
  dragged-home loops have the same image, so injectivity identifies the loops, and conjugating
  back by the chosen paths identifies the arrows.
* **Surjective on $\pi_1$ $\Rightarrow$ full.** Drag the target arrow home with the chosen
  paths, pull it back through $\varphi$, and push it out again.
* **Connected target $\Rightarrow$ essentially surjective**, for free: everything is isomorphic
  to the image of the basepoint.

Fully faithful plus essentially surjective is an equivalence. $\blacksquare$
</details>

The following script exercises this on genuine examples, including three groups of the *same
order* — $\mathbb{Z}/8$, $D_4$, $Q_8$ — whose aspherical spaces are pairwise non-equivalent.

For a cyclic source the classification becomes a classical statement: homotopy classes of maps
$K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1) \to K(H,1)$ are conjugacy classes of elements of order dividing $n$, and for
the circle itself one recovers *free homotopy classes of loops = conjugacy classes*.

{{demo:1}}

## 7. The sharp counterexample

Now break it. Take a **point** and a **two-point discrete space**. Both have trivial
fundamental group; obviously they are not homotopy equivalent. That much is the standard
warning that connectedness matters. But the failure is far worse than it looks.

> **Theorem.** In a totally disconnected space *every* homotopy group vanishes. Hence the
> one-point space and the discrete two-point space have isomorphic homotopy groups in **every
> degree**, yet are not homotopy equivalent.

<details>
<summary><b>Why every homotopy group dies (three-line proof)</b></summary>

A cube $[0,1]^N$ is connected. The continuous image of a connected set is connected. A
connected subset of a totally disconnected space is a single point. So every based cube map is
constant — equal to the basepoint, since the boundary goes there — and therefore any two are
equal, let alone homotopic. $\blacksquare$
</details>

So **no** family of homotopy groups whatsoever can be a complete invariant without a
connectivity hypothesis. The tower is blind to one thing only: the set of components.

---

## 8. The repair: what the complete invariant really is

The missing datum is $\pi_0$, and it is the *only* missing datum.

> **Decomposition.** Every 1-type is the disjoint union of its connected components, each of
> which is a $K(G,1)$.
>
> **Gluing.** A disjoint union of connected 1-types is determined by its indexing set together
> with the fundamental groups of the pieces.
>
> **Complete invariant.** Two homotopy 1-types are homotopy equivalent **iff** there is a
> bijection between their sets of connected components under which the fundamental groups of
> corresponding components are isomorphic.

Equivalently: the complete invariant is the **multiset of fundamental groups of the
components**. Build two 1-types out of pieces and test it yourself — shuffle the pieces (still
equivalent), change one group (no longer equivalent), delete a component (no longer
equivalent), or load the point-versus-two-points preset to see the sharp counterexample as a
special case of the theorem.

{{interactive_demo:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>How the two halves fit together</b></summary>

For the decomposition, take the full sub-1-type on each isomorphism class of points. The
assembly map back into the whole is *faithful* (arrows never leave a component), *full* (each
component is full), and *essentially surjective* (every point lies in its own component) — so
it is an equivalence.

For the gluing, an equivalence must permute the summands, because points in different
components are never joined; that gives the bijection of index sets, and Whitehead's theorem
gives the isomorphisms of fundamental groups. Conversely, component-wise equivalences assemble
into a global one as soon as the index bijection is available. $\blacksquare$
</details>

The decision procedure below implements exactly this: split into components by a union–find
pass over the arrows, reduce each component to a canonical invariant of its fundamental group,
and compare the sorted multisets.

{{algorithm:1}}

---

## 9. What you now know

* An aspherical space **is** its fundamental group: nothing is lost, nothing is added.
* A map between two of them **is** a homomorphism, up to conjugacy; every homomorphism occurs,
  and the number of homomorphisms per homotopy class is the index of a centraliser.
* A map inducing an isomorphism of fundamental groups **is** a homotopy equivalence — the
  one-dimensional Whitehead theorem.
* Drop connectedness and the whole homotopy tower fails to classify, with a point versus two
  points as the sharpest possible witness.
* Restore it with $\pi_0$: the pair (set of components, fundamental groups of the components) is
  a complete invariant of arbitrary homotopy 1-types.

Where to go next: [crossed modules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossed_module) do for
2-types what groups do for 1-types, adding $\pi_2$, an action, and a cohomological
$k$-invariant; and the [Whitehead theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitehead_theorem) in
its general form is the statement whose one-dimensional shadow you have just seen proved in
full.

/-! ## The conjugation action on `Hom(G,H)` -/

section ConjAction

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] {H : Type*} [Group H]

/-- Conjugation action of the target group on homomorphisms. -/
instance conjSMul : SMul H (G →* H) :=
  ⟨fun u φ => ((MulAut.conj u).toMonoidHom).comp φ⟩

@[simp] theorem conj_smul_apply (u : H) (φ : G →* H) (a : G) :
    (u • φ) a = u * φ a * u⁻¹ := rfl

instance conjMulAction : MulAction H (G →* H) where
  one_smul φ := by ext a; simp
  mul_smul u v φ := by ext a; simp [mul_assoc]

/-- Two homomorphisms lie in the same orbit of the conjugation action exactly when
they are conjugate, i.e. exactly when they are identified in `conjSetoid`. -/
theorem mem_orbit_iff_conj (φ ψ : G →* H) :
    ψ ∈ MulAction.orbit H φ ↔ ∃ u : H, ∀ a, ψ a = u * φ a * u⁻¹ := by
  rw [MulAction.mem_orbit_iff]
  exact ⟨fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨u, fun a => by rw [← hu, conj_smul_apply]⟩,
         fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨u, MonoidHom.ext fun a => (hu a).symm⟩⟩

/-- **The stabiliser of a homomorphism is the centraliser of its image.** -/
theorem stabilizer_eq_centralizer (φ : G →* H) :
    MulAction.stabilizer H φ = Subgroup.centralizer (Set.range φ) := by
  ext u
  simp only [Subgroup.mem_centralizer_iff, MulAction.mem_stabilizer_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h' x hx
    obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := hx
    have := congr_arg (· g) h'
    simp [conj_smul_apply] at this
    have h := congr_arg (· * u) this
    simp at h
    exact h.symm
  · intro h'
    ext g
    simp [conj_smul_apply]
    have := h' (φ g) (Set.mem_range_self g)
    rw [mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul]
    exact this.symm

/-- The orbit of `φ` under conjugation is in bijection with the coset space of the
centraliser of its image. -/
noncomputable def orbitEquivQuotientCentralizer (φ : G →* H) :
    MulAction.orbit H φ ≃ H ⧸ Subgroup.centralizer (Set.range φ) :=
  (MulAction.orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer H φ).trans
    (Quotient.congrRight (by rw [stabilizer_eq_centralizer φ]; exact fun _ _ => Iff.rfl))

/-- The number of homomorphisms conjugate to `φ` is the index of the centraliser of
the image of `φ`. -/
theorem card_orbit_eq_index_centralizer (φ : G →* H) :
    Nat.card (MulAction.orbit H φ) = (Subgroup.centralizer (Set.range φ)).index := by
  have h1 := Nat.card_congr (orbitEquivQuotientCentralizer φ)
  rw [h1, Subgroup.index]

end ConjAction

section Fibres

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D] {d₀ : D}

/-- Two homomorphisms are realised by homotopic maps exactly when they lie in the
same conjugation orbit. -/
theorem natIso_realize_iff_mem_orbit (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (d₀ : D) (φ ψ : Aut c →* Aut d₀) :
    Nonempty (realize hC d₀ φ ≅ realize hC d₀ ψ) ↔ ψ ∈ MulAction.orbit (Aut d₀) φ := by
  rw [realize_natIso_iff_conj]
  rw [MulAction.mem_orbit_iff]
  exact ⟨fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨u, MonoidHom.ext fun a => by rw [hu, conj_smul_apply]⟩,
         fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨u, fun a => by rw [← hu, conj_smul_apply]⟩⟩

/-- **Fibres of the classification.**  The homomorphisms inducing a fixed homotopy
class of maps of 1-types are exactly a coset space of the centraliser of the image;
in particular their number is the index of that centraliser. -/
theorem card_homs_natIso_realize (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (φ : Aut c →* Aut d₀) :
    Nat.card {ψ : Aut c →* Aut d₀ // Nonempty (realize hC d₀ φ ≅ realize hC d₀ ψ)}
      = (Subgroup.centralizer (Set.range φ)).index := by
  have : {ψ : Aut c →* Aut d₀ // Nonempty (realize hC d₀ φ ≅ realize hC d₀ ψ)} =
      {ψ : Aut c →* Aut d₀ // ψ ∈ MulAction.orbit (Aut d₀) φ} := by
    congr 1 with ψ
    exact natIso_realize_iff_mem_orbit hC d₀ φ ψ
  rw [this]
  exact card_orbit_eq_index_centralizer φ

end Fibres

/-- In a groupoid every endomorphism is invertible, so the endomorphism monoid of

/-! ## Chosen paths in a connected groupoid -/

section BasePaths

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C}

/-- A chosen isomorphism from the basepoint to each object of a connected
groupoid, normalised so that the basepoint receives the identity. -/
noncomputable def basePath (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (d : C) : c ≅ d :=
  open Classical in
  if h : c = d then eqToIso h else (hC d).some

@[simp] theorem basePath_self (hC : ConnectedAt C c) : basePath hC c = Iso.refl c := by
  simp [basePath]

conjugating with the chosen paths. -/

  basePath hC X ≪≫ (Groupoid.isoEquivHom X Y).symm g ≪≫ (basePath hC Y).symm

@[simp] theorem loopOf_hom (hC : ConnectedAt C c) {X Y : C} (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    (loopOf hC g).hom = (basePath hC X).hom ≫ g ≫ (basePath hC Y).inv := rfl

  simp only [loopOf, basePath_self]
  simpa using Equiv.symm_apply_apply (Groupoid.isoEquivHom c c) a

  simp only [loopOf]
  show _ = Iso.trans _ _
  simp [Groupoid.isoEquivHom, Iso.trans]

  simp only [loopOf]
  have h : (Groupoid.isoEquivHom X X).symm (𝟙 X) = Iso.refl X := Equiv.symm_apply_apply (Groupoid.isoEquivHom X X) (Iso.refl X)

  obj _ := d₀
  map g := (φ (loopOf hC g)).hom

  map_comp f g := by rw [loopOf_comp, map_mul]; rfl

  rw [realize_map_aut]

section Conjugacy

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D]

/-- Intertwining two automorphisms by a third is the same as conjugating them. -/
theorem aut_hom_comp_eq_iff {E : Type u'} [Category.{v'} E] {e₀ : E} (p q u : Aut e₀) :
    p.hom ≫ u.hom = u.hom ≫ q.hom ↔ q = u * p * u⁻¹ := by
  constructor

    have h2 : u * p = q * u := Iso.ext h
    have h3 := congrArg (fun z => z * u⁻¹) h2
    simpa [mul_assoc] using h3.symm
  · intro h
    subst h
    have h4 : u * p = u * p * u⁻¹ * u := by group
    exact congrArg Iso.hom h4

`[X, K(H,1)] ≃ Hom(π₁ X, H)/conjugation`. -/
theorem realize_natIso_iff_conj (hC : ConnectedAt C c) (d₀ : D) (φ ψ : Aut c →* Aut d₀) :

    refine ⟨α.app c, fun a => ?_⟩
    have naturality := α.hom.naturality a.hom
    simp only [realize_map_aut, realize_obj] at naturality
    have key := aut_hom_comp_eq_iff (φ a) (ψ a) (α.app c)
    have h : (φ a).hom ≫ (α.app c).hom = (α.app c).hom ≫ (ψ a).hom := by simpa using naturality

  · rintro ⟨u, hu⟩
    rw [natIso_iff_conjugating_iso hC]
    refine ⟨u, fun a => ?_⟩
    dsimp [realize]
    rw [loopOf_aut hC]
    have hψ := hu a
    exact aut_hom_comp_eq_iff (φ a) (ψ a) u |>.mpr hψ

variable {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] {c : C} {D : Type u'} [Groupoid.{v'} D]

theorem faithful_of_injective_mapAut (F : C ⥤ D) (hC : ConnectedAt C c)
